vars.prTitle: ref(stacktraces): only report in-app frames as the crash frame
vars.prBody: When an error has no in-app frame in its top stacktrace, `get_crash_frame_from_event_data` falls back to the top system/library frame, so issue locations end up pointing at framework internals (dispatch loops, `__call__` wrappers) that users can't act on. This makes it return only in-app frames and `None` otherwise, so the UI shows no location instead of a misleading one.
vars.injectPatch:
diff --git a/src/sentry/stacktraces/processing.py b/src/sentry/stacktraces/processing.py
index 1029acb..d30ff12 100644
--- a/src/sentry/stacktraces/processing.py
+++ b/src/sentry/stacktraces/processing.py
@@ -505,12 +505,13 @@ def get_crash_frame_from_event_data(data, frame_filter=None):
     Return the highest (closest to the crash) in-app frame in the top stacktrace
     which doesn't fail the given filter test.
 
-    If no such frame is available, return the highest non-in-app frame which
-    otherwise meets the same criteria.
+    Frames from third-party/system code are never reported as the crash frame:
+    pointing users at e.g. a framework's dispatch loop is more confusing than
+    showing no location at all.
 
     Return None if any of the following are true:
-        - there are no frames
-        - all frames fail the given filter test
+        - there are no in-app frames
+        - all in-app frames fail the given filter test
         - we're unable to find any frames nested in either event.exception or
           event.stacktrace, and there's anything other than exactly one thread
           in the data
@@ -524,20 +525,14 @@ def get_crash_frame_from_event_data(data, frame_filter=None):
         if threads and len(threads) == 1:
             frames = get_path(threads, 0, "stacktrace", "frames")
 
-    default = None
     for frame in reversed(frames or ()):
-        if frame is None:
+        if frame is None or not frame.get("in_app"):
             continue
-        if frame_filter is not None:
-            if not frame_filter(frame):
-                continue
-        if frame.get("in_app"):
-            return frame
-        if default is None:
-            default = frame
+        if frame_filter is not None and not frame_filter(frame):
+            continue
+        return frame
 
-    if default:
-        return default
+    return None
 
 
 def lookup_frame_cache(keys):
vars.goldenComments: [{"comment": "get_crash_frame_from_event_data is not only used for the issue location: `get_fingerprint_value` in src/sentry/grouping/utils.py resolves the custom fingerprint / title-template variables `{{ function }}`, `{{ stack.abs_path }}`, `{{ stack.filename }}`, `{{ stack.module }}` and `{{ stack.package }}` through it. For any event whose top stacktrace has no in-app frame (common for native/mobile and for SDKs where in_app is not set), these variables now resolve to `<no-function>`, `<no-module>`, etc. instead of the crashing frame's values. Projects with fingerprint rules like `stack.function:... -> {{ function }}` therefore get their fingerprints changed for existing issues (regrouping into new issues) and, worse, all such events collapse into a single group with the same `<no-function>` fingerprint, merging unrelated crashes; `{{ function }}` in custom titles (expand_title_template) degrades the same way.", "severity": "High"}]
